title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 2°) of a numbered construction. In 1°) Grothendieck considers a Lie group G acting differentiably on R^n with the origin fixed. G then acts on the space S_0^# of rays (the half-lines R^+ v). He builds G~ as the set of pairs (g, lift of the action of g to the universal cover S~_0 of S_0^#).

Here G = GL(2,R)^{±1} = {u : det u = ±1}, acting on C ≅ R^2. The ray space is identified with the unit circle U via z ↦ R^+ z. Choosing the base point 1 ∈ U identifies the pointed universal cover with the exponential cover R → U, t ↦ exp(2iπt).

A lift of a homeomorphism of the circle to its universal cover is determined by where it sends one point. So lifting the action of u to some ũ amounts to choosing t ∈ R with exp(2iπt) = u(1)/|u(1)|, that is, choosing an argument of u(1) (formula 12).

Applying the general construction gives an extension (13): 1 → Z → GL(2,R)^{±1~} → GL(2,R)^{±1} → 1. Its kernel Z consists of the deck translations t ↦ t+n. Restricting to the neutral component SL(2,R) gives (14): 1 → Z → SL(2,R)~ → SL(2,R) → 1.

Proposition: SL(2,R)~ is connected (presumably also simply connected) and homeomorphic to R^3. The next page proves this. U = SO(2) ↪ SL(2,R) is a homotopy equivalence, and topologically SL(2,R) ≅ U × R^2 (Iwasawa/polar decomposition). So it suffices that the preimage of U is its universal cover R, and this follows from (12).

Following corollaries:
- Finite cyclic subgroups of SL(2,R) lift to infinite cyclic subgroups whose generator ϖ satisfies ϖ^n = the generator of the kernel.
- Elements of determinant −1 act on the kernel and on the centre by inversion. The full extension (13) is therefore non-central, while (14) is central.

Purpose (within the 'Longue Marche' sequel): this sets up the universal central extension of SL(2,R) and its orientation-reversing enlargement. The likely aim is to pull them back to GL(2,Z)/SL(2,Z), getting the braid-group-type extension SL(2,Z)~ ≅ B_3 (preimage in SL(2,R)~) and its GL version. These are the fundamental groups of the genus-1 Teichmüller/moduli objects (M_{1,1} with a tangential base point), which enter the Teichmüller tower and Galois-action analysis.
errors: Previous page formula (10) writes the action on U as z ↦ u(z)/|z|; it should be u(z)/|u(z)|. Formula (12) on this page uses the correct normalization u(1)/||u(1)||.

The Proposition as transcribed only says 'connexe'. For the proof's conclusion (homeomorphic to R^3) one also uses, and gets, simple connectivity. The statement is correct either way: SL(2,R) ≅ S^1 × R^2, so its universal cover ≅ R × R^2.

Minor: for det u = −1 the lift ũ is an orientation-reversing homeomorphism of R. The pair description still works, but the resulting extension (13) is not central. Grothendieck notes this himself on the next page (Cor. 2).

ideas.what: Construction of G~ for a group acting on R^n fixing 0, as lifts of the action on the circle (sphere) of rays to its universal cover; specialization to GL(2,R)^{±1} giving the extension 1→Z→GL(2,R)^{±1~}→GL(2,R)^{±1}→1
ideas.modern_name: Group of lifts of circle homeomorphisms; universal covering group of SL(2,R) and its extension to the orientation-reversing component (pullback of the lift extension of Homeo(S^1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Ghys's exposition of Homeo~(S^1); standard Lie theory)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse in this form; related genus-1 discussion of B_3 / SL(2,Z) occurs in Esquisse d'un programme and later Lochak–Schneps work

ideas.what: SL(2,R)~ is homeomorphic to R^3 (via SO(2) ≅ U homotopy equivalence and SL(2,R) ≅ U × R^2)
ideas.modern_name: Universal cover of SL(2,R); Iwasawa decomposition

ideas.what: Explicit parametrization of the lift of u by a choice of argument t of u(1) (formula 12)
ideas.modern_name: Rotation-number / argument-lift description of the universal cover (cf. Milnor–Wood, Ghys)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely standard Lie-group and covering-space material: the universal cover of SL(2,R) and its orientation-reversing enlargement, presented via lifts of the action on rays. It is preparatory to the genus-1 (B_3 / SL(2,Z)~) discussion, but nothing on this page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'rev. universel de S_0 pointé au dessus de e_0' — S_0 here stands for the ray space S_0^#, and the base point is the ray through 1 (point 1 of U).
'un relèvement de u_{S^1}' should likely read 'un relèvement de u_{S_0^#} en ũ' (the action of u on the ray space).
In (11) the parenthetical reads '(≃ S_0)' and '(↦ R^+ exp 2iπt)', i.e. the map to rays.
'Gl(2,R)^{±1 ~}' denotes the tilde group G~. The struck word before 'neutr.' is 'Propos', and the phrase reads 'au-dessus de la composante neutre SL(2,R)'.
Proposition likely reads 'Le groupe Sl(2,R)~ est connexe, et est homéomorphe à R^3'; the struck word is probably 'contractile'.
